We're seeing a major regression in our production traffic to Redwood starting ~08:45 PT this morning. Latency (p95) jumped from ~120ms to 700-900ms, and error rate climbed to ~10% 503s. This is impacting our checkout flows.

I've attached a short log tail and a pcap from a single client instance (client-log-20270516.txt, client-pcap-20270516.pcap). Initial look from our SRE shows a lot of truncated header frames and mid-stream connection resets.

Can your team triage? We're open to a short call immediately.

Subject: RE: Production: sudden RTT spikes + 10% 503s since 08:45 PDT

Quick technical summary from the on-call SDK team after an initial pass on the artifacts:

- Reproducer notes: The attached pcap shows repeated TCP segments where the HTTP/1.1 header block is split across packets (partial header lines). Our 1.4.7 streaming parser assumes header lines are atomically available when invoking the framing logic; when headers are split at the TCP layer the parser sometimes treats the header set as malformed and tears down the stream instead of buffering until next segment. That behavior produces mid-request 5xx/503s and adds extra retries leading to p95 RTT inflation.

- Hypothesis: a regression in the incremental header-assembly path introduced in 1.4.7 to improve tail latency; it reduces internal buffering thresholds and exposed edge cases for split headers.

- Immediate mitigations we can push:
  1) Route affected customers to a fallback pool with the older 1.4.6 runtime (no code change required on customer's side) — this reduces the error rate quickly.
  2) Temporarily increase connection buffering and per-request assembly timeouts at the edge (config flip) to allow header reassembly.
  3) Provide a small client-side config you can set while we prepare a patch: sdk.transport.buffering=false (forces conservative buffering on the client).

- Longer-term: we have a parser patch that handles fragmented header lines robustly; attaching a preliminary patch and test pcap. I recommend we ship 1.4.8 hotfix ASAP and coordinate a safe rollout.

Attachments: client-pcap-20270516.pcap, sdk-fix-parse-1.4.8.patch

—Sean Gallagher
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Production: sudden RTT spikes + 10% 503s since 08:45 PDT

Hi Alice / team —

Thanks for the quick data. Vanessa and I discussed the immediate customer-facing steps:

1) Workaround (customer action, low risk): set sdk.transport.buffering=false in your runtime config. This will avoid the aggressive trimming behavior on the client and reduce immediate 503s.
2) If you prefer not to change client config, we can flip the route for your account to run against the 1.4.6 fallback pool on our side. This is the fastest zero-downtime option.
3) We’re preparing a 1.4.8 hotfix with the header-assembly fix; ETA for release candidate: ~3–4 hours, full rollout after canary verification.

We will also provide a small credit for the affected window; Vanessa, can you advise on discount/credit?

Proposed external message: short explanation, immediate mitigation recommended, ETA for hotfix, and offer of credit. I can send the external message once Vanessa confirms wording.

—Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production: sudden RTT spikes + 10% 503s since 08:45 PDT — status and exec note

Alice —

Quick status update and next steps after our internal work today:

- Root cause: a regression in SDK 1.4.7's streaming parser that can prematurely treat split/fragmented header lines as malformed, causing connection tears and 5xx responses under certain TCP segmentation patterns.
- Immediate impact: we observed a peak error rate ~10% across a small subset of your fleet; p95 latency rose due to retries.
- What we did for you:
  • We routed Nimble Retail to our 1.4.6 fallback pool at 11:30 PT yesterday which reduced errors to baseline within ~10 minutes.
  • Provided a customer-side workaround (sdk.transport.buffering=false) that you can enable to avoid client-side aggressive trimming.
  • SDK 1.4.8 hotfix (parser fix) is validated in canary as of 16:30 PT and scheduled for phased rollout.

Next steps and asks from us:
- Vanessa (me) requests approval for a goodwill credit to Nimble Retail for the affected window. Suggested amount: 25% of the impacted-day invoice. This will be handled by finance once approved.
- Engineering request: Marcus/Sean to proceed with expedited 1.4.8 rollout after canary.

Alice, I will send a short exec-friendly summary for your leadership if you'd like — please let me know. We take this seriously and will follow up with a full postmortem when the rollout is complete.

Thanks for the patience and the quick data — it made triage much faster.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Lead, Enterprise Success — Redwood Inference
